metadata.title: KD-FixMatch: Knowledge Distillation Siamese Neural Networks

extraction_notes.note: The custom heuristic environment wraps an algorithm2e float that latex_facts.py does not report, so its pseudocode was extracted by hand as an algorithm with one step per If/ElseIf/Else branch (confidence 0.8).
theorem (external) or not a node: the sentence cites the robustness of symmetric losses without a precise statement; kept as a cited result at 0.65.

Experimental setup (backbone, optimizer, hyperparameters, the five compared methods (a)-(e)), the data tables, the introduction's contribution list and the conclusion's restatement of results were not made nodes.

Observations (b)-(d) are items of one run-on list separated by semicolons, so each claim starts at its item label rather than a sentence start (finishing-step warning kept); AP4 is a pseudocode body ending in a closing brace, not a sentence.
Each empirical observation is followed by a 'The (possible) reason is ...' explanation; these explain rather than justify the table-backed claims, so no proof nodes were made for them.

subsec:exp-public.section: Experiments on Four Public Data Sets

nodes.name: Knowledge distillation
nodes.statement: Knowledge distillation \cite{GH15a} is a well-known model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a pre-trained, larger teacher model to a smaller student model.
differentia: transfers knowledge from a pre-trained, larger teacher model to a smaller student model

nodes.name: Noisy Student
nodes.statement: In Noisy Student, once the student is found to be better than the teacher, the pseudo labels are updated by the current student, and a new student is re-initialized. This procedure is then repeated several times.
nodes.statement_short: Iterative self-training: when the student beats the teacher, relabel with the student, re-initialize a new student, and repeat.

nodes.name: Sequential training must wait for the teacher
nodes.statement: However, this approach requires waiting for the teacher to be well-trained before generating highly confident pseudo labels for the student's training.

nodes.name: Siamese neural network (SNN)
nodes.statement: The core neural network architecture for {\sl FixMatch} is SNN which consists of two identical weight-sharing classifier networks, a teacher and a student.
differentia: consists of two identical weight-sharing classifier networks, a teacher and a student

nodes.name: Network and dimension notation
nodes.statement: Assume that $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$ is a standard neural network with softmax output layer, $\boldsymbol \theta \in \Re^n$ is a long vector, $\ell$ is the number of training examples, $K$ is the number of the classes, and $n$ is the total number of the parameters of $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$.
nodes.statement_short: $f_\theta$ is a softmax network with parameters $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^n$; $\ell$ training examples, $K$ classes.

nodes.name: FixMatch optimization problem
nodes.statement: We define the optimization problem for {\sl FixMatch} to be \begin{equation} \min_{\boldsymbol \theta}\ f(\boldsymbol \theta), \text{where}\ f(\boldsymbol \theta) = \frac{1}{2C} \boldsymbol \theta^T \boldsymbol \theta + \frac{1}{\ell} \sum_{i=1}^\ell \xi(\boldsymbol \theta;{\boldsymbol x}^i,{\boldsymbol y}^i) \end{equation} $C > 0$ is the parameter to avoid overfitting by regularization, ${\boldsymbol x}^i$ is the $i$th input image, and ${\boldsymbol y}^i$ is the label vector of ${\boldsymbol x}^i$.
nodes.statement_short: Minimize an $\ell_2$-regularized average loss $\frac{1}{2C}\theta^T\theta + \frac1\ell\sum_i \xi(\theta;x^i,y^i)$ over network weights.

nodes.name: FixMatch objective
nodes.statement: \min_{\boldsymbol \theta}\ f(\boldsymbol \theta), \text{where}\ f(\boldsymbol \theta) = \frac{1}{2C} \boldsymbol \theta^T \boldsymbol \theta + \frac{1}{\ell} \sum_{i=1}^\ell \xi(\boldsymbol \theta;{\boldsymbol x}^i,{\boldsymbol y}^i)
nodes.label: fixmatch-obj

nodes.name: Label vector (one-hot)
nodes.statement: In addition, if ${\boldsymbol x}^i$ belongs to the $s$th class, the label vector, ${\boldsymbol y}^i$, is $[\underbrace{0, \ldots, 0}_{s-1}, 1, 0, \ldots, 0]^T \in \Re^K$.

nodes.name: Labeled and unlabeled sets $S_l$, $S_u$
nodes.statement: However, training examples for SSL consists of both a set of the labeled data, $S_l$, and a set of the unlabeled data, $S_u$.

nodes.name: FixMatch loss function
nodes.statement: Therefore, {\sl FixMatch} uses teacher inside SNN to generate pseudo labels as label vectors for ${\boldsymbol x}^i, i \in S_u$ and then the loss function, $\xi$, in \eqref{fixmatch-obj} can be defined as follows: \begin{equation} \xi(\boldsymbol \theta;{\boldsymbol x}^i,{\boldsymbol y}^i) = \begin{cases} \xi_l\left({\boldsymbol y}^i, f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{w})\right) & \text{if}\ \ i \in S_{l},\\ \lambda_u \xi_u(\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i, f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{s})) & \text{if}\ \ i \in S_{u}, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i$ is the pseudo label vector of ${\boldsymbol x}^i, i \in S_u$, $\lambda_u$ is a pre-defined parameter, ${\boldsymbol x}^i_w$ is the weakly augmented image of ${\boldsymbol x}^i$, ${\boldsymbol x}^i_s$ is the strongly augmented image of ${\boldsymbol x}^i$, $\xi_l$ is a loss function for the labeled data, and $\xi_u$ is a loss function for the unlabeled data.
nodes.statement_short: Per-example loss: supervised loss $\xi_l$ on weakly augmented labeled inputs, weighted $\lambda_u\xi_u$ on strongly augmented unlabeled inputs against teacher pseudo labels.

nodes.name: FixMatch per-example loss
nodes.statement: \xi(\boldsymbol \theta;{\boldsymbol x}^i,{\boldsymbol y}^i) = \begin{cases} \xi_l\left({\boldsymbol y}^i, f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{w})\right) & \text{if}\ \ i \in S_{l},\\ \lambda_u \xi_u(\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i, f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{s})) & \text{if}\ \ i \in S_{u}, \end{cases}
nodes.label: fixmatch-loss

nodes.name: Cross-entropy (CE) as $\xi_l$
nodes.statement: In \cite{KS20a}, $\xi_l$ in \eqref{fixmatch-loss} is the standard cross-entropy (CE) function to measure the difference between $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{w})$ and its label vector ${\boldsymbol y}^i$.

nodes.name: Teacher in SNN
nodes.statement: For $\xi_u$ in \eqref{fixmatch-loss}, when the input of $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$ is ${\boldsymbol x}^i_w$, $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$ is considered as the teacher and $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{w})$ is $\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i$ of ${\boldsymbol x}^i$.
nodes.statement_short: With weakly augmented input, $f_\theta$ acts as the teacher and its output is the pseudo label $\hat y^i$.

nodes.name: Student in SNN
nodes.statement: Conversely, $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$ is considered as the student when the input of $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$ is ${\boldsymbol x}^i_s$.

nodes.name: Confidence-thresholded unlabeled loss
nodes.statement: However, in order to reduce label noise, we only choose the highly confident pseudo labels whose maximum value are greater than or equal to a pre-defined threshold $\tau > 0$ and thus $\xi_u$ in \eqref{fixmatch-loss} can be defined as follows: \begin{equation} \mathbb{1}(\max(\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i) \geq \tau ) \xi_{u}(\text{OHL}(\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i), f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{s})), \end{equation} where $\mathbb{1}$ is an indicator function and OHL is a function mapping a softmax pseudo label vector to its one-hot label vector.
nodes.statement_short: Unlabeled loss is applied only when the pseudo label's max probability is at least $\tau$, using its one-hot version as target.

nodes.name: Confidence-masked unlabeled loss
nodes.statement: \mathbb{1}(\max(\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i) \geq \tau ) \xi_{u}(\text{OHL}(\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i), f_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{s})),
nodes.label: fixmatch-filter

nodes.name: FixMatch
nodes.statement: After the loss function, $\xi$, in \eqref{fixmatch-obj} is prepared, back-propagation is applied to update the weights in $f_{\boldsymbol \theta}$ and thus both teacher and student are updated simultaneously by minimizing \eqref{fixmatch-obj}.
nodes.statement_short: Train the SNN by back-propagation on objective (1), updating teacher and student simultaneously.

nodes.name: Simultaneous training suffers from early label noise
nodes.statement: For the method where teacher and student are trained simultaneously, there is no need to wait for the teacher's training procedure to complete before the student's can begin. However, in the early stage, heavy label noise or insufficient correct pseudo labels generated by the immature teacher may affect the generalization ability of the student model.
nodes.statement_short: Simultaneous training avoids waiting for the teacher, but early immature-teacher label noise can hurt the student.

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch outer and inner SNN
nodes.statement: We propose an algorithm called {\sl KD-FixMatch}, which contains an outer SNN, $f^{\text{outer}}$, and an inner SNN, $f^{\text{inner}}$.

nodes.name: Trusted Pseudo Label Selection
nodes.statement: Similar to \eqref{fixmatch-filter}, we first choose a pre-defined threshold, $\tau^{\text{select}}$, and choose the pseudo labels whose maximum value is greater than or equal to $\tau^{\text{select}}$. Then, we extract the latent representations\footnote{ The representations are derived from the layer before the last layer. } of the unlabeled data which has passed the $\tau^{\text{select}}$ selection. We do a deep embedding clustering \cite{JX16a, XY21a} on the representations and choose the unlabeled data whose clustering results are consistent with their predicted class.\footnote{ The predicted class is the index of the maximum value of $\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i$. } Finally, the indices of the chosen unlabeled data form $T_u$.
nodes.statement_short: Keep outer-SNN pseudo labels above $\tau^{select}$ whose deep-embedding cluster agrees with the predicted class; their indices form $T_u$.

nodes.name: Inner SNN trusted pseudo labels
nodes.statement: Following \eqref{fixmatch-filter}, we choose the pseudo labels whose maximum value is greater than or equal to a pre-defined threshold, $\tau^{\text{inner}} > 0$, to be inner SNN's trusted pseudo labels.
differentia: whose maximum value is greater than or equal to a pre-defined threshold, $\tau^{\text{inner}} > 0$

nodes.name: Merging Conflict Pseudo Labels
nodes.statement: \uIf{$\max\left(f^{\text{inner}}_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{w})\right) \geq \tau^{\text{inner}}$}{ $\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i \leftarrow f^{\text{inner}}_{\boldsymbol \theta}({\boldsymbol x}^i_{w})$ } \uElseIf{$i \in T_u$}{ $\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i \leftarrow {\boldsymbol y}^{i,\text{outer}}$ } \Else{ $\hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i \leftarrow {\boldsymbol 0}$ }
nodes.statement_short: Use the inner SNN's pseudo label if confident, else the outer SNN's label if $i\in T_u$, else the zero vector.

nodes.name: Inner SNN generalizes better
nodes.statement: The main idea is that the inner SNN intuitively has better generalization ability than the outer SNN since it has more reliable pseudo labels in the early stage.

nodes.name: Robustness of symmetric loss functions
nodes.statement: The widely used loss functions in robust learning is symmetric loss functions \cite{NM13a,AG17a} which has been proven to be robust to noisy labels.
nodes.origin_citation: Manwani & Sastry 2013; Ghosh et al. 2017 (NM13a, AG17a)
conclusions: has been proven to be robust to noisy labels

nodes.name: Symmetric loss function
nodes.statement: Assume that $f$ is a standard neural network with softmax output layer. From \cite{AG17a}, a loss function $\xi$ is called symmetric if it satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^K \xi(f({\boldsymbol x}), {\boldsymbol e}_k) = M,\ \forall {\boldsymbol x} \in X,\ \forall f,$ where $K$ is the number of classes, $X$ is the feature space, $f$ is a function mapping an input ${\boldsymbol x}$ to a softmax output ${\boldsymbol y}$, $M$ is a constant value, and ${\boldsymbol e}_k = [\underbrace{0, \ldots, 0}_{k-1}, 1, 0, \ldots, 0]^T \in \Re^K$.
differentia: $\sum_{k=1}^K \xi(f({\boldsymbol x}), {\boldsymbol e}_k) = M,\ \forall {\boldsymbol x} \in X,\ \forall f,$
nodes.statement_short: A loss is symmetric if its sum over all one-hot targets $e_k$ is a constant $M$ for every input and network.

nodes.name: Examples of robust loss functions (MAE, SCE, NCE)
nodes.statement: Mean absolute error (MAE) \cite{CJW85a}, symmetric cross-entropy (SCE) \cite{YW19a}, and normalized cross-entropy (NCE) \cite{XM20a} are examples of robust loss functions.
nodes.origin_citation: CJW85a; Wang et al. 2019 (YW19a); Ma et al. 2020 (XM20a)

nodes.name: Inner SNN optimization problem
nodes.statement: For the inner SNN, the optimization problem and loss functions are the same as \eqref{fixmatch-obj}, \eqref{fixmatch-loss}, and \eqref{fixmatch-filter} except that we substitute $f$, $C$, $\xi_l$, $\lambda_u$, $\xi_u$, and $\tau$ with $f^{\text{inner}}$, $C^{\text{inner}}$, $\xi^{\text{inner}}_l$, $\lambda^{\text{inner}}_u$, $\xi^{\text{inner}}_u$, and $\tau^{\text{inner}}$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Inner SNN uses objective (1)-(3) with its own $f, C, \xi_l, \lambda_u, \xi_u, \tau$ (superscript inner).

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch
nodes.statement: Given a labeled data, $S_l$, and an unlabeled data, $S_u$\; 1: Initialize an outer SNN, $f^{\text{outer}}$, and train it with $S_l$ and $S_u$ by using back-propagation to solve \eqref{fixmatch-obj}\; 2: Generate pseudo labels for $S_u$ using the well-trained $f^{\text{outer}}$\; 3: Select a trusted index subset $T_u$ from $S_u$\; 4: Choose CE or a robust loss function to be $\xi^{\text{inner}}_u$\; 5: Initialize an inner SNN, $f^{\text{inner}}$, and train it with not only the labeled and unlabeled data but also the unlabeled data with trusted pseudo labels, $({\boldsymbol x}^i, \hat{{\boldsymbol y}}^i), i \in T_u$\; 6: Return the well-trained $f^{\text{inner}}$\; \caption{KD-FixMatch}
nodes.statement_short: Train an outer SNN with FixMatch, select trusted pseudo labels $T_u$, then train an inner SNN with labeled, unlabeled and trusted pseudo-labeled data.
nodes.label: alg:os-fixmatch

nodes.name: Symmetric cross-entropy (SCE)
nodes.statement: The formula of SCE is $\alpha \times \text{CE} + \beta \times \text{RCE}$ and RCE stands for reverse cross-entropy.

nodes.name: Reverse cross-entropy (RCE)
nodes.statement: Assume that $H({\boldsymbol q}, {\boldsymbol p})$ is a standard CE function given two distributions, ${\boldsymbol q}$ (ground truth distribution) and ${\boldsymbol p}$ (distribution from the softmax neural network output), RCE can be defined as: $H({\boldsymbol p}, {\boldsymbol q})$.

nodes.name: FixMatch beats Baseline
nodes.statement: (a) {\sl FixMatch} is better than {\sl Baseline} for all the cases.
nodes.section: 4.1 Experiments on Four Public Data Sets
conclusions: {\sl FixMatch} is better than {\sl Baseline} for all the cases.

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch beats FixMatch
nodes.statement: (b) {\sl KD-FixMatch} is better than {\sl FixMatch} for all the cases.
nodes.section: 4.1 Experiments on Four Public Data Sets
conclusions: {\sl KD-FixMatch} is better than {\sl FixMatch} for all the cases.

nodes.name: Diminishing improvement with more labeled data
nodes.statement: (c) Comparing to {\sl FixMatch}, the more labeled data we use, the less improvements we have for {\sl KD-FixMatch}.
nodes.section: 4.1 Experiments on Four Public Data Sets
conclusions: Comparing to {\sl FixMatch}, the more labeled data we use, the less improvements we have for {\sl KD-FixMatch}.

nodes.name: KD-FixMatch-SCE slightly better than KD-FixMatch-CE
nodes.statement: (d) {\sl KD-FixMatch-SCE} has slightly better model performance than {\sl KD-FixMatch-CE} in most of the cases even without grid search for the two parameters, $(\alpha, \beta)$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Experiments on Four Public Data Sets
conclusions: {\sl KD-FixMatch-SCE} has slightly better model performance than {\sl KD-FixMatch-CE} in most of the cases
